summary:
BEYOND THE SILENCE: The Machines We Left Behind, The Discoveries They Left With Us

Project BIFROST  is an interactive, cinematic web experience that explores six remarkable NASA space missions and the machines behind them: the Apollo Lunar Module, Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner Rover, Opportunity Rover, Pioneer 10, and Kepler Space Telescope.

Instead of presenting information through static slides, the project allows visitors to explore three environments — the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space. Each artifact has a short documentary-style story, visual representations, 3D exploration, and scientific information with references.

The project addresses the challenge by transforming the history and scientific contributions of space exploration technologies into an engaging, accessible digital archive. It highlights how machines continue to contribute to human knowledge long after their missions end.

Its purpose is to make space exploration history more interactive, understandable, and inspiring, while preserving the scientific legacy of the machines we sent beyond Earth.
details:
Beyond the Silence

NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 | Challenge: Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars

Team: Dimensione X | Members: Erai Arasi, Sania Afroz, Priyanka Ayali

1. Summary

Since the 1960s, NASA has left hardware across the solar system: landers and rovers on the Moon and Mars, and probes still travelling away from Earth. Much of it finished its mission long ago and fell silent. Beyond the Silence is an interactive web experience that gives these machines a voice. A visitor chooses a destination, meets the spacecraft that was left there, rotates a 3D model of it, and reads the story of what it achieved and what became of it.

2. The Problem

Abandoned spacecraft are usually remembered as a line in a mission archive. Their engineering, their discoveries and the people behind them are scattered across many NASA pages and are hard for a general audience to find or feel connected to. The challenge asks for storytelling that keeps this hardware from being forgotten.

3. Our Solution

Beyond the Silence is a single-page web application organised around three destinations on a "Choose Your Exploration" screen: the Moon, Mars and Deep Space. Each destination lists the artifacts left there. Each artifact page has the same structure, so visitors always know where to look:

* 3D model: a model the visitor can drag to rotate and scroll or pinch to zoom.

* Scientific record: key facts such as developer, launch or mission dates, instruments and notable firsts.

* Mission history: a dated timeline from launch to the end of contact or the last use.

* Storytelling: the story of each artifact, told as a narrative.

* NASA sources: links to the NASA pages the content is drawn from, and a note on details the sources do not cover.

Artifacts

Moon Apollo Lunar Module, Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV)

Mars Sojourner Rover, Opportunity Rover

Deep Space Pioneer 10, Kepler Space Telescope

5. Technical Overview

* Front end: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, delivered as a static web page with no server required.

* 3D viewer: interactive models embedded in each artifact page with drag, scroll and pinch controls.

* Content: mission facts, timelines and sources taken from NASA resources listed on the challenge page.

* Navigation: home screen, destination pages, artifact pages, and a Next button that moves through each artifact's sections.

* Development tools: the app was developed in Visual Studio Code with help from Claude, an AI assistant made by Anthropic. Images were created with Google Gemini.

6. Design Choices

A dark, starlit interface and a serif title style give the project a quiet, memorial tone that suits its subject. The same page layout is reused for every artifact to keep the experience simple for non-experts. Each page separates the verified scientific record from the narrative, so the story never replaces the facts.

7. Data Sources and Credits

* NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 resources for the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten".

* NASA mission pages for each artifact.

* AI assistance: Claude (Anthropic) and Visual Studio Code were used during development, and Google Gemini was used to create images.

Conclusion

8.These machines are silent, but their stories are not finished. Beyond the Silence turns scattered archive material into an experience people can explore, so the equipment NASA left behind stays remembered.
